analyst_view.overall: Crystal Palace are bottom with 7 points after five straight league defeats, the latest a 3-2 loss at Coventry. Thomas Frank was appointed on 16 November in place of Pierre Sage, and this is his first home league game, three days after a Europa League home game against Real Sociedad on Thursday. Jean-Philippe Mateta (last game of a three-match league ban) and Yeremy Pino (suspended) both miss it, so Jorgen Strand Larsen is expected to lead the attack; Sarr and Tomiyasu could be back, and Riad is out. Hull are 11th and beat Brighton 2-0 with two late Oli McBurnie goals, but Tim Iroegbunam has a hamstring problem (the numbers count him as out) and several others, including Morita, are missing. The numbers already count Pino's ban and Jarred Gillett's card record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals: 1.0 for Palace and 1.2 for Hull. They already take Pino's ban off Palace and Iroegbunam off Hull. Mateta also misses this, but he had scored only once in five games this season, so his absence costs little. A new manager could lift Palace, but the European game three days earlier could drain them, so I stay at about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.5 corners, 5.6 for Palace at home, already counting Palace conceding plenty of corners lately and Hull winning more. Frank's first home game should see Palace push forward, which fits that split, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.0 cards, already raised because both sides have been booked more than usual lately, and they count Jarred Gillett's average card rate. It is a tense game for a bottom side, but nothing new points to more cards than that, so I stay at about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 26.4 shots, 16.4 of them from Palace. Palace play Real Sociedad on Thursday night, only three days before, while Hull have had a full week, and the numbers do not count that congestion. Without Mateta and Pino, Palace also lose two of their usual shooters, so I take about 3% off, to about 25.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 9.2 shots on target, 5.8 for Palace, helped by how many Hull have allowed lately. Palace's tired legs after the Europa League game are not counted, but Pino's ban already is, so I make only a small 2% cut, to about 9.0.
